# Edmund Carrow

## Overview

- **Age:** Thirteen years old (Volume 5)  <sub>[v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012)</sub>
- **Origin:** Hollowmere, Glen St. Agnes  <sub>[v5 c3 P0](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolboy  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Walt  <sub>[v5 c3 P28](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0028)</sub>; Miss Edmund  <sub>[v5 c17 P9](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0009)</sub>

## Appearance

Edmund is a handsome boy with well-shaped features, straight black hair, and large, deep gray eyes that express a range of emotions. He has pale skin that blushes deeply when he feels ashamed or angry. He is taller than average for his age, with long limbs, but lacks physical strength and is considered somewhat frail.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c17 P8](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0008), [v5 c17 P19](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0019), [v5 c17 P25](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0025)_

## Personality

Edmund is a sensitive, imaginative, and deeply poetic boy who loves nature, literature, and dreaming. He is quiet and often absorbed in his own thoughts, preferring reading to rough sports, which leads some peers to consider him timid or 'girly.' Though he despises violence and dreads physical pain, he possesses a strong sense of honor and surprising courage when defending those he cares about. He is deeply empathetic, averse to seeing any living thing suffer, and possesses a flair for dramatic storytelling.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c3 P15](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0015), [v5 c3 P20](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0020), [v5 c17 P16](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0016), [v5 c17 P19](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0019), [v5 c17 P25](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0025), [v5 c17 P28](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0028), [v5 c29 P1](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0001), [v5 c35 P20](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0020)_

## History

Edmund grew up at Hollowmere alongside his siblings, spending much of his childhood playing in Fern Hollow and exploring the woods. Uninterested in typical boyish sports, he spent his time reading poetry and inventing imaginative names for natural landmarks, such as calling a birch tree the 'White Lady.' In school, he was teased by peers like Dan Coyle for writing poetry instead of doing arithmetic. When Dan Coyle insulted Grace Ashdown and his mother, Edmund confronted Dan and beat him in a fight, proving his courage despite his aversion to violence. He later decided to face his fear of pain by having his aching tooth extracted. As he grew into his early teens, he began writing poetry seriously in an exercise book, aspiring to follow in the footsteps of poets he admired.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P0](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0000), [v5 c3 P4](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0004), [v5 c3 P5](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0005), [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P15](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0015), [v5 c4 P43](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0043), [v5 c17 P9](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0009), [v5 c17 P11](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0011), [v5 c17 P17](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0017), [v5 c17 P28](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0028), [v5 c29 P2](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0002)_

## Background by volume

- Grew up at Hollowmere in Glen St. Agnes as the son of Dr. Hugh Carrow and Nell Carrow  <sub>[v5 c3 P0](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0000), [v5 c5 P0](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0000), [v5 c5 P8](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0008)</sub>
- Suffered from severe toothaches as a child  <sub>[v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001), [v5 c17 P8](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0008)</sub>

## Quotes

> The angel of flowers has traveled across the earth today, summoning the blossoms. Those blue wings of his are visible to me on that hill near the forest.  <sub>[v5 c3 P20](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0020)</sub>

> A coincidence is what you are!  <sub>[v5 c17 P10](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0010)</sub>

> You were insulted by him, and my mother was insulted by him as well. Dan, tonight following school.  <sub>[v5 c17 P17](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0017)</sub>

> I felt extremely scared. However, I do not intend to feel scared again, sir. Experiencing fear about troubles is more unpleasant than those troubles are. I plan to request that father drive me to Kettlebridge tomorrow so I can have my tooth pulled.  <sub>[v5 c17 P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)</sub>

> The Piper is drawing closer, he is closer than he was on the evening I previously saw him. He has his long, shadowy cloak blowing about him. He pipes—he pipes—and we are forced to follow—Kit and Rupert and Tobias and I—around and around the globe. Listen—listen—are you unable to hear his wild music?  <sub>[v5 c35 P15](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0015)</sub>
